content.title: Telefonica looks to M&A to give European telecoms broader vision
content.summary: LONDON (Reuters) -Spanish telecoms group Telefonica is looking to buy telecom assets and free up resources by selling its Spanish-speaking Latin American assets, as CEO Marc Murtra plots a broader vision for Europe's telco sector.  The group is eyeing assets in Germany, the UK, Spain and Brazil, Murtra told Reuters as he prepares his first strategic plan for Telefonica after taking the helm in January.  Regulators have long pushed back against mergers between European operators, fearing a few dominant players would be able to increase prices and margins to the disadvantage of the consumer, but Murtra argues that Europe's market is too fragmented.

content.title: Spanish government cancels contract with Telefonica for using Huawei gear
content.summary: MADRID (Reuters) -The Spanish government has cancelled a fibre-optic service contract with Telefonica over the use of equipment made by China's Huawei, the Digital Transformation Ministry said, amid concerns in Europe that such gear may pose a security risk.  The report by El Pais newspaper earlier on Friday also said  that through this 10 million-euro ($11.7 million) contract, Telefonica was to supply fibre-optic connections to a series of government institutions including the Defence Ministry.  Telefonica's Chief Operating Officer Emilio Gayo told Reuters last month that the company was "reducing its exposure to Huawei" in Spain to comply with EU recommendations to telecom operators to phase out Huawei-made devices over security concerns.

content.title: Telefonica renewed one Huawei 5G contract in Spain until 2030, report says
content.summary: MADRID (Reuters) -Telefonica renewed a contract with Chinese manufacturer Huawei to supply equipment for its 5G mobile core network for retail customers in Spain until 2030, El Pais newspaper reported on Thursday, citing unnamed industry sources.  Telefonica renewed that contract in late 2024 and, in early 2025, it awarded to rival manufacturer Nokia a contract for 5G core for its service to companies and government institutions, El Pais said.
